newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: SOCCER-ETHIOPIA STAY IN NATIONS CUP DESPITE DEFECTIONS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ETHIOPIA STAY IN NATIONS CUP DESPITE DEFECTIONS.

text.p: Ethiopia, who failed to fulfil an African Nations Cup fixture with Morocco earlier this month when 16 players sought political asylum in Italy, have been allowed to stay in the competition.
It was widely expected that CAF, African soccer's ruling body, would disqualify Ethiopia from the Cup when its exective committee met on Thursday.
But CAF president Issa Hayatou said the Ethiopians would keep their place.

"After weighing up all the evidence the committee felt it was a case of 'force majeure' -- the Ethiopian F.A. had fulfilled all their criteria. It was not their fault the players got off the plane," he said.
"Morocco have been given the opportunity to name six dates on which the re-arranged match can be played. All the other matches in the qualifying group should go ahead as scheduled."
Of the 16 who left the plane in Rome en route from Addis Abbaba to Morocco, five have since returned to Ethiopia, because of fears of reprisals against their families.
But CAF did disqualify the central African republic for failing to play their Nations Cup qualifier in Sierra Leone earlier this month.

Hayatou said investigations had shown there were no problems with any flights from the African republic's capital of Bangui to Freetown, the capital of Sierra Leone, and that all the players were ready for the flight.
A decision taken by the Government prevented the squad from flying and as a result the disqualification was justified, he said.
He also said that clubs from Liberia and Benin competing in the CAF Cup had been disqualified for not submitting their players' licences by the January 15 deadline.
